instructions: Calm, warm science-documentary narrator. Natural, engaging pace, clear articulation, a brief pause between sentences.

lines.text: Each frame shows where a language model's feedback loop settles, for one setting of steering strength and temperature: thirty-two trajectories, drawn in the coordinates of the model's own states and colored by the word being written. The red dot marks our place on the map of chaos.
On the left of the map, the loop simply repeats: is it, is it.
Then a three-step loop takes over and doubles its period, three, six, twelve, until the attractor dissolves into chaos.
The cascade runs backward, and the loop returns to repeating text.
Further right, windows of repeating text alternate with chaos, and from one window to the next the loop changes by one pair of words.
Here the chaos is strongest: the states spread over the whole attractor, and the text never settles.
Then order returns abruptly, in a window where the loop repeats an eight-step text.
Now we climb in temperature at a steering strength of 0.075, and then descend through the whole column.
Here chaos and repeating text alternate densely: in three of every five frames of this column, none of the thirty-two trajectories settles into a loop.
Every one of these shapes is the same small language model, feeding its own output back to itself.
